purpose: Read-only repository case studies for the UI/UX specialist capability (three charters + proposed skill ui_ux-research-design-engineering). Records what each repo demonstrates, license/lifecycle posture, and implementation lessons. No code was executed; all inspection via GitHub API/primary docs on 2026-11-20.
verification: License SPDX and lifecycle fields verified via GitHub API (repos/{owner}/{repo}, /releases/latest, /contents) on 2026-11-20. NOASSERTION means a custom license GitHub cannot classify (for W3C repos: W3C Document/Software licenses) - read the LICENSE file before excerpting.

cases.name: w3c/wcag
cases.demonstrates: WCAG 2.x normative text (guidelines + success criteria) maintained as a versioned repo; Understanding/Techniques live in sibling repos. The standard itself is inspectable infrastructure - every conformance claim can be pinned to exact criterion text and version.
implementation_lessons: Quote criteria by number + version + URL; never paraphrase normative text in audit reports.
WCAG 2.2 retired 4.1.1 Parsing - audit templates must be version-aware.
Techniques are informative; conformance is against success criteria only.

cases.name: w3c/aria
cases.demonstrates: ARIA 1.3 Working Draft development in the open (new roles suggestion/comment/mark, aria-description, braille attributes, aria-notify). Companion specs (Core-AAM, AccName, HTML-AAM) show the pipeline from markup to platform accessibility APIs.
implementation_lessons: ARIA 1.2 (Rec 2023-06) is the production baseline; 1.3 features must not be cited as requirements and need real-AT testing before use.
Accessible Name Computation explains divergent screen-reader output: aria-label overrides content; empty alt ('') differs from missing alt.
Spec issues are public - support matrices (a11ysupport.io) beat spec-reading for deployment decisions.

cases.name: w3c/wai-aria-practices (APG)
cases.demonstrates: The pattern unit of accessible UI: each pattern = role structure + states/properties + full keyboard interaction script + working example + regression tests. ~30 patterns (dialog, combobox, tabs, menu, grid, treeview, carousel, disclosure...).
implementation_lessons: ARIA supplies semantics, zero behavior: the APG keyboard script (arrow keys, Home/End, Enter/Space, Escape, roving tabindex) is the author's obligation and the top hand-rolled-widget failure.
W3C's own caveat: example code demonstrates the spec; it is not production-hardened. Re-test with NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver before shipping copies.
Where a vetted library (Radix/React Aria/Ariakit) implements the pattern, prefer it over hand-rolling.

cases.name: w3c/wai-website
cases.demonstrates: Docs-as-code production of WAI guidance: ARRM (role/responsibility mapping), tutorials, older-users resources, curricula. Shows accessibility guidance maintained with the same PR/review discipline as code.
implementation_lessons: ARRM is the governance bridge: decompose WCAG into designer/developer/content/QA checkpoints instead of assigning 'accessibility' to one person.
Treat accessibility documentation as versioned artifacts with review, not wiki folklore.

cases.name: design-tokens/community-group (DTCG)

license.spdx: NOASSERTION (W3C Community CLA for spec text)

cases.demonstrates: Vendor-neutral design-token interchange: $value/$type/$description, groups, {alias} references, resolver-based theming. First stable version after 5 years of drafts; reference implementations Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio, Terrazzo; adopted by Figma, Penpot, Sketch, Framer.
implementation_lessons: It is a W3C Community Group Final Report, NOT a W3C standard - say 'DTCG 2025.10', never 'the W3C token standard'.
Version tokens by module date (2025.10) so tool support claims are checkable; tool support is still partial (e.g., Style Dictionary v5 support in progress).
Three-tier architecture (primitive -> semantic -> component) makes theming/dark-mode/high-contrast an alias swap, not a rebuild.

cases.name: radix-ui/primitives
cases.demonstrates: 59 single-responsibility packages: interaction behaviors (focus-scope, roving-focus, dismissable-layer, focus-guards, portal, presence, announce) packaged separately from the visible components (dialog, select, menu). Accessibility behavior as composable, unstyled primitives - consumers bring their own tokens/CSS.
implementation_lessons: The existence of dedicated focus/roving/dismissable packages shows where hand-rolled widgets fail: keyboard navigation, focus trapping, outside-click dismissal, portal layering.
Unstyled primitives are the dominant fix for the WebAIM finding that pages with ARIA average more errors than pages without - adopt encoded behavior, restyle freely.
Per-primitive versioning lets consumers pin risk; monorepo discipline keeps 59 packages coherent.

cases.name: adobe/react-spectrum (React Aria)
cases.demonstrates: Layered architecture across 12 package groups: @react-aria (behavior hooks incl. keyboard/pointer/screen-reader quirks), @react-stately (state machines), @react-spectrum (styled Adobe skin), @internationalized (dates, numbers, collation, RTL), react-aria-components (unstyled composition layer).
implementation_lessons: Separate behavior, state, presentation, and internationalization - each is independently testable and replaceable.
i18n is an infrastructure layer (@internationalized), not a per-component afterthought: RTL, calendars, number formats must be designed into primitives.
Behavior hooks absorb browser/AT quirks (Safari VO, touch vs. pointer) that product teams rediscover expensively.

cases.name: ariakit/ariakit
cases.demonstrates: Store-based headless components shipped for both React and Solid from shared store packages (15 packages: ariakit-store + react/solid bindings + tailwind integration). Framework-portable state stores with controlled/uncontrolled duality.
implementation_lessons: Component state can be framework-agnostic (plain stores) with thin framework bindings - reuse logic across React/Solid instead of re-implementing per framework.
0.x semver signals API evolution: pin versions and read changelogs before upgrading in a design system.

cases.name: floating-ui/floating-ui
cases.demonstrates: Positioning solved once, correctly: platform-agnostic `core` compute -> `dom` binding -> framework packages (react, vue, react-native, utils, devtools). Middleware pipeline (offset, flip, shift, arrow, autoUpdate, size, hide) composes collision handling.
implementation_lessons: Overlay geometry (tooltips, popovers, menus) is a solved subproblem - hand-rolled positioning fails on viewports, scroll containers, and RTL; delegate to the core+middleware model.
Core logic with no DOM dependency is testable in isolation and portable to canvas/native.

cases.name: storybookjs/storybook
cases.demonstrates: The story as the unit of design-system work: documentation, visual review, interaction tests, and the a11y addon (axe-core per story) all target the same artifact. Framework-agnostic workshop; controls/args make component states enumerable.
implementation_lessons: Stories force explicit states (default/hover/focus/disabled/loading/error/empty/overflow/RTL) - the states teams forget in specs become the story matrix.
Accessibility testing belongs in the component dev loop (axe per story), not as a pre-release audit.
A published Storybook is living documentation and the design/engineering contract surface.

cases.name: d3/d3
cases.demonstrates: Visualization as data joins + scales + selections + generators - a grammar of graphics at DOM level rather than chart templates. Maximal expressiveness; the author owns every perceptual and accessibility decision.
implementation_lessons: Scales encode the Cleveland-McGill decision: choosing a linear position scale vs. an arc is choosing the accuracy tier of the reading.
D3 gives no accessibility by default: SVG title/desc, role=img, tabular fallback, and keyboard interaction are author responsibilities - pair with an explicit a11y checklist.
Low-level power means low-level failure modes: transition junk, non-semantic SVG, and unlabeled axes are common in the wild.

cases.name: apache/echarts
cases.demonstrates: Declarative option-object charting with a built-in accessibility surface (`aria` component: generated chart descriptions, decal patterns for color-independent encoding) - contrast with D3's build-everything model.
implementation_lessons: Batteries-included viz can ship a11y features (decals, auto-descriptions) - evaluate whether generated descriptions actually state findings or just restate structure.
Declarative configs are diffable/testable design artifacts; theme objects act like token sets for charts.

cases.name: microsoft/playwright
cases.demonstrates: Cross-browser automation whose recommended locators (getByRole, getByLabel, getByText) mirror the accessibility tree - test ergonomics that push teams toward correct ARIA semantics. Traces/videos/screenshots as evidence artifacts.
implementation_lessons: Role-based locators make tests assert semantics, not CSS hooks - a test suite becomes an executable accessibility contract.
Pair with @axe-core/playwright for per-page rule checks inside real flows (login, checkout), which static scans cannot reach.
Automated checks still cover only the mechanical ~30-40% of WCAG issues; keep manual keyboard/AT passes in the release gate.

cases.name: dequelabs/axe-core
cases.demonstrates: WCAG compiled into executable checks: 155 rule files under lib/rules, check implementations under lib/checks, and standards data (aria-roles, aria-attrs, html-elms, dpub/graphics roles, css-colors) under lib/standards. Rules tagged to WCAG criteria/levels; engineered for zero false positives on reported violations.
implementation_lessons: The rule->criterion tag mapping is the audit trail: every automated finding can cite the SC it tests.

LICENSE is MPL-2.0 WITH the Exhibit B 'Incompatible With Secondary Licenses' notice (verified 2026-11-20): embedding is fine and modification triggers file-level source disclosure, and Exhibit B means axe-core files cannot be combined into a GPL-licensed work - wrap, don't fork, for product use.
'Needs review' vs 'violation' distinction in results encodes the automated/manual boundary honestly.

cases.name: pa11y/pa11y
cases.demonstrates: CLI/CI-first accessibility testing (HTML_CodeSniffer engine) with pa11y-ci, pa11y-dashboard, and pa11y-webservice companions. Demonstrates the batch/CI reporting model as a complement to axe-core's embedded engine model; LGPL-3.0-only licensing (link/dynamically load rather than embed into proprietary source without compliance review).
implementation_lessons: Runner choice is a license + workflow decision, not just accuracy: axe (MPL-2.0+Exhibit B, embedded), pa11y (LGPL-3.0-only, CLI/service) have different obligations.
Two engines produce non-identical counts - report engine + version + rule set with every metric, and triage disagreements manually.
CLI/CI tools test URLs, not flows - authenticated/multi-step journeys still need Playwright-style drivers.

cases.name: nvaccess/nvda

license.spdx: GPL-2.0-or-later WITH two exceptions (Non-GPL Components in Plugins and Drivers; Microsoft Distributable Code) - copying.txt

cases.demonstrates: The free, open-source Windows screen reader used in manual accessibility testing. Copying.txt is the authoritative license (GPL-2.0+ with plugin/driver and Microsoft-code exceptions) - an example of reading the project's own license file rather than trusting the GitHub API (which returns NOASSERTION).
implementation_lessons: Manual AT testing is part of the conformance method, not optional: pair NVDA (Windows) + VoiceOver (macOS/iOS) + keyboard-only passes; automated engines cannot judge announcement quality.
GPL-2.0-or-later with exceptions: fine to use as a test tool; do not embed or link NVDA code into proprietary products without legal review.
Speech-viewer and log output make AT sessions recordable evidence artifacts for audit trails.

cases.name: realworld-apps/realworld (canonical; formerly gothinkster/realworld)

license.spdx: MIT (Thinkster 2021 / c4ffein 2026; GitHub API returns NOASSERTION - LICENSE verified directly)

cases.demonstrates: 'The mother of all demo apps': one full-stack spec (Conduit) implemented across many frontend/backend stacks, with a shared spec (specs/) that includes API contract and E2E test expectations. Demonstrates a shared acceptance suite: the same observable behavior tested against independent implementations.
implementation_lessons: Canonical URL is realworld-apps/realworld - the gothinkster/realworld link is the legacy alias; pin canonical identity + commit SHA like any external dependency.
Shared E2E specs decouple behavior claims from stack: usability/a11y E2E suites (axe runs, keyboard scripts, target-size probes) can ride on the same pattern.
A realistic CRUD app is a better usability-lab substrate than toy demos: real auth, forms, feed pagination, and error states.

cases.name: mapbox/pixelmatch
cases.demonstrates: The smallest correct visual-regression primitive: anti-aliasing-aware pixel diffing with a perceptual threshold, used inside larger VRT stacks. Demonstrates that 'looks broken' is measurable (diff pixel count + threshold) but never sufficient - diffs need human triage for meaning.
implementation_lessons: Visual regression metrics: report diff-pixel count, threshold, and viewport matrix; a threshold is a design decision, not a default.
Pixel diffs detect change, not regressions - pair with intentional-change baselines and human review of flagged screenshots.

cases.name: garris/BackstopJS
cases.demonstrates: Config-driven visual regression testing across viewport scenarios (headless Chromium): scenario matrices (selectors, viewports, interactions) with approve/report workflow. Demonstrates VRT as a reviewable design-system release gate.
implementation_lessons: Scenario config = the design system's explicit state matrix (viewport x component state); drift in coverage is visible in the config.
Approval workflow encodes human sign-off on visual change - the tool proposes, the human approves baselines.

cases.name: eugenkiss/7guis

license.spdx: NONE (no license file - all rights reserved; cite/link only, do not copy code)

cases.demonstrates: 7GUIs: seven benchmark GUI programming tasks (counter, temperature converter, flight booker, timer, CRUD, circle drawer, cells) that isolate interaction-state challenges (undo/redo, validation, bidirectional data flow, layout constraints) from framework noise. A task spec for comparing implementations and for prototyping-lab exercises.
implementation_lessons: Interaction complexity is separable from visual design: the same seven tasks expose state-management and focus/keyboard weaknesses regardless of styling.
No license file means all-rights-reserved by default: reference and re-implement from the task descriptions; never vendor the code.
Low commit activity is healthy for a frozen benchmark - lifecycle must be judged against artifact type.

cases.name: penpot/penpot
cases.demonstrates: The open-source design & prototyping tool: SVG-native document model (designs are inspectable markup, not proprietary blobs), self-hostable, token support aligned with DTCG, plugin system, MCP surface, WebGL renderer (render-wasm) for performance.
implementation_lessons: An open document model (SVG) makes design files diffable, scriptable, and agent-readable - the open alternative to proprietary handoff.
Self-hosting matters for regulated teams evaluating design tooling; MPL allows commercial self-host use with file-level copyleft.
Penpot + DTCG tokens + Style Dictionary + headless components = fully open design-to-code pipeline.

cases.name: style-dictionary/style-dictionary

lifecycle.note: repo moved from amzn/ org to style-dictionary/ org - update references; API redirect confirmed 2026-11-20

cases.demonstrates: Token build pipeline: DTCG JSON in -> platform outputs (CSS custom properties, Swift, Kotlin, JS) via transform chains. Tokens as compiled artifacts with one source of truth.
implementation_lessons: Treat token changes as versioned commits with CI build + visual regression on generated output, not manual handoff.
DTCG support is still completing in v5 - verify the specific token types a version supports before committing a taxonomy.
Org moves break deep links: pin dependency + documentation URLs and re-verify periodically.

cases.name: alphagov/govuk-frontend
cases.demonstrates: Public-sector design system: Nunjucks components behind research-backed service patterns (GOV.UK Service Manual: 'ask one thing per page', 'check answers', error-message writing standards). Accessibility engineered for the broadest public including low digital literacy.
implementation_lessons: Patterns (how to ask for a thing, how to write an error) outlive components - ship pattern guidance, not just a component library.
Plain language is an accessibility feature: GDS treats content design as part of the component contract.
Services used by everyone must work with no assumptions about device, bandwidth, or expertise - the extreme-case test bed.

cases.name: a11yproject/a11yproject.com
cases.demonstrates: Community-maintained, plain-language operationalization of WCAG (checklist + how-tos + myths). Demonstrates translating normative criteria into daily development tasks for non-specialists.
implementation_lessons: A curated checklist is an on-ramp, not conformance - always map checklist items back to SC numbers.
Community resources need maintenance governance (review dates on posts) to avoid stale technique advice.

cases.name: mdn/content

license.spdx: NOASSERTION (CC-BY-SA 2.5 for content, CC0 for code samples)

cases.demonstrates: 14,000+ pages of web platform docs including the definitive ARIA/HTML attribute and CSS references; docs-as-code with public review.
implementation_lessons: MDN is the reference layer between specs (what's normative) and tutorials (what's expedient) - cite it for API behavior, W3C for requirements.
Content license (CC-BY-SA) differs from code-sample license (CC0) - attribution rules differ per reuse type.

recreated_project_labs.title: Recreate the APG modal dialog from scratch, then replace it with Radix/React Aria
recreated_project_labs.task: Hand-build the APG dialog pattern (focus trap, Escape, aria-modal, restore focus), test with keyboard + one screen reader, enumerate failures; then swap in a vetted primitive and diff the behavior list.
recreated_project_labs.evaluates: Understanding that ARIA adds no behavior; where focus management fails; why vetted primitives win.

recreated_project_labs.title: Recreate a three-tier DTCG 2025.10 token pipeline
recreated_project_labs.task: Author primitive->semantic->component tokens with aliases; build to CSS via Style Dictionary; implement dark + high-contrast themes as resolver/alias swaps only; verify all text pairs pass 4.5:1 with the contrast script.
recreated_project_labs.evaluates: Token tiering, theming without rebuilds, contrast-in-the-token-layer.

recreated_project_labs.title: Recreate a GOV.UK-style form flow
recreated_project_labs.task: Build one-thing-per-page flow with check-answers and error summary; write error messages to GDS standards; run axe + keyboard + 200% zoom + 320px reflow; then attempt the same flow as a single dense page and compare task times in a 5-user hallway test.
recreated_project_labs.evaluates: Pattern vs. component thinking; plain language; measured (not asserted) usability.

recreated_project_labs.title: Recreate the Cleveland-McGill / Heer-Bostock judgment experiment
recreated_project_labs.task: Render the same dataset as bar (position/length), pie (angle), and bubble (area) charts; run 10 colleagues through 12 comparison questions; measure error rates per encoding; publish the mini-study with method + raw data.
recreated_project_labs.evaluates: Evidence-based encoding choice; running a tiny controlled study honestly (n, method, limits).

recreated_project_labs.title: Recreate an accessibility CI gate
recreated_project_labs.task: Wire axe-core into Playwright (role-locator tests through a real flow) and into Storybook (a11y addon); record rule IDs -> WCAG SC mapping; document which manual checks (focus order, alt quality, AT pass) remain outside the gate.
recreated_project_labs.evaluates: Executable accessibility contracts; honest automated/manual split.

recreated_project_labs.title: Recreate a motion system with reduced-motion parity
recreated_project_labs.task: Prototype transitions (drawer, toast, list reorder, route change) with 200-500ms transform/opacity motion; implement prefers-reduced-motion fallbacks that replace travel/scale with fades while keeping feedback semantics; verify 2.2.2 pause control on anything auto-moving >5s.
recreated_project_labs.evaluates: Reduce-not-remove; CSS vs. JS motion guard paths; vestibular-safe feedback.

recreated_project_labs.title: Recreate a dual-engine accessibility scan with comparable metrics
recreated_project_labs.task: Run axe-core (via @axe-core/playwright) and pa11y against the same RealWorld (Conduit) routes. Metrics to record: engine+version, violations per rule ID mapped to WCAG 2.2 SC, 'needs review' counts, route coverage, and a manually triaged disagreement table (engine A flags / engine B silent and vice versa). Deliverable includes the explicit statement of what neither engine can judge (reading order, alt-text quality, focus logic) and a 10-minute NVDA keyboard pass log.
recreated_project_labs.evaluates: Engine/version reporting discipline; automated-vs-manual boundary honesty; WCAG 2.2 (not 3.0) criterion mapping.

recreated_project_labs.title: Recreate a visual-regression release gate with measurable thresholds
recreated_project_labs.task: Build a BackstopJS scenario matrix (3 viewports x component states incl. focus/error/loading) over a Storybook; justify the pixelmatch threshold; produce a run report with diff-pixel counts and before/after screenshots; run a human approval round and record which diffs were accepted as intentional vs. fixed as regressions.
recreated_project_labs.evaluates: Thresholds as decisions; human-in-the-loop baseline approval; state-matrix coverage.

recreated_project_labs.title: Recreate the RealWorld shared-spec pattern for UX behavior
recreated_project_labs.task: Take the RealWorld spec's shared expectations and extend them with a UX-behavior layer: role-based locators for every interactive element, tab-order script for the auth flow, target-size probe (24px WCAG 2.5.8 floor vs. 44pt Apple / 48dp Android commitments), and per-route axe runs. Run the identical suite against two different stack implementations and compare behavior deltas, not code.
recreated_project_labs.evaluates: Stack-independent behavior verification; role-locator accessibility contracts; measured target-size compliance.

recreated_project_labs.title: Recreate two 7GUIs tasks and measure interaction quality
recreated_project_labs.task: Implement CRUD and Circle Drawer from the 7GUIs task descriptions (no code copying - repo has no license): full keyboard operation, undo/redo with focus restoration, validation with accessible error messages. Metrics: keystroke-level model (KLM) prediction vs. measured expert task time, error counts, and a 5-participant hallway test with task success + SEQ per task.
recreated_project_labs.evaluates: Interaction-state correctness (undo/focus/validation); KLM-vs-measured calibration; honest small-n reporting.
